crypto/x509/trust#

Verifying certificate chains against trusted roots.

Version: v1.0.0

Synopsis#

let verified = VerifiedCertificateChain(
    chain: CertificateChain([leaf, intermediate]),
    trust: SystemTrustStore(),
    host: DnsCertificateIdentity(HostName("example.com")),
    at: SystemClock().instant(),
    purpose: CertificatePurpose("1.3.6.1.5.5.7.3.1"),        // TLS server
);
verified.leaf();         // CertificateVerificationFailed says why it is not trusted

Description#

Verifying certificate chains against trusted roots.

Roots come from the system, from given certificates or from PEM text; an empty store trusts nothing. Only the TLS server and client purposes are verified.

Public API#

role TrustStore#

role TrustStore

Explicit local root selection; an empty store means no trust anchors and never selects system defaults. The role grants no filesystem capability.

object SystemTrustStore#

object SystemTrustStore does TrustStore

Only result() reads selected system CA locations. Every call acquires a new immutable snapshot, allowing its owning client/policy to choose its lifetime. The operating system's trusted roots, read each time they are asked for.

object PemTrustStore#

object PemTrustStore does TrustStore

Strict CERTIFICATE-only PEM input, snapshotted at construction. It does not read files or validate CA/chain/purpose/time/hostname/revocation policy. Input <=8 MiB, <=1024 roots, total DER <=16 MiB; no secret text in failures.

PemTrustStore.PemTrustStore#

PemTrustStore(source is string)

Roots in PEM text: CERTIFICATE blocks only, at most 1024; InvalidTrustStore otherwise.
